TEXT_D:
Summary of 2019 UK policy proposals (max 500 words)

- Europe and constitutional reform
  - Revoke Article 50 to remain in the EU if winning a majority; otherwise back a referendum with an option to remain.
  - Protect freedom of movement; enfranchise long‑term EU residents in UK elections; reform electoral registration to automatic inclusion.
  - Electoral reform to Single Transferable Vote for MPs and councils; votes at 16; overseas constituencies; House of Lords reform; stricter transparency and regulation of political advertising and lobbying; citizens’ assemblies on major issues.
  - Devolution to nations and English regions with a written federal constitution and matched funding powers.

- Economy, business and work
  - £130bn infrastructure plan (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing), plus a £50bn regional rebalancing programme and Green Investment Bank.
  - Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapult centres; regional innovation funds; support creative industries.
  - Skills Wallets of £10,000 per adult for lifelong learning; broaden apprenticeship levy to a Skills and Training Levy.
  - Corporate governance reforms: employee board representation; due‑diligence duties on human rights/environment; binding shareholder votes on executive pay.
  - Tax: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; align capital gains with income tax; tougher anti‑avoidance and improved Digital Services Tax.
  - Work: new “dependent contractor” status with core rights; living wage approach; flexible working from day one; stronger enforcement; fair gig‑economy pensions and zero‑hours protections.

- Education and childcare
  - Free, high‑quality childcare: 35 hours/week, 48 weeks/year for ages 2–4 and from 9–24 months for working parents; increased early years funding and staff training; expanded Children’s Centres.
  - Reverse school funding cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; clear repairs backlog.
  - Replace SATs and narrow league tables with broader assessment; new inspectorate; stronger SEND funding.
  - “Curriculum for life,” arts protection, careers links, better vocational routes.
  - Further/higher education: +£1bn for colleges, restore maintenance grants, stronger student mental health, review finance; Young People’s Premium.

- Environment, energy and transport
  - Net‑zero by 2045; at least 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking.
  - Ten‑year nationwide home insulation and zero‑carbon heat programme; zero‑carbon new buildings by 2021, rising to Passivhaus by 2025.
  - Circular economy law: phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; right‑to‑repair; 70% recycling target.
  - Nature recovery targets; 60m trees/year; peatland and marine protection; £5bn flood programme; sustainable farming reform.
  - Transport: Clean Air Act; all new cars/vans electric by 2030; more ULEZs; rail electrification by 2035; fare freeze for a parliament; expand light rail, buses, cycling/walking; fix fares and access.

- Health, social care and public health
  - +1p on Income Tax raising £7bn/year for NHS and social care; £10bn capital; plan for a dedicated Health and Care Tax; integrate services and end automatic tendering.
  - Mental health: new waiting‑time standards; 24/7 crisis care; perinatal support; free prescriptions for chronic conditions; student mental health charter; tighter gambling rules.
  - Prevention: obesity strategy; right to clean air; minimum unit pricing for alcohol; PrEP on NHS; decriminalise abortion UK‑wide with safe access zones; drug policy reform including a regulated cannabis market.

- Social security, housing and communities
  - Reform Universal Credit: first payment in 5 days; end two‑child limit and benefit cap; higher work allowances incl. second earner; replace sanctions with incentive‑based approach; abolish bedroom tax; align LHA with rents; reinstate Independent Living Fund; right to food; end fuel poverty by 2025.
  - Pensions: retain triple lock; remedy for women born in the 1950s.
  - Housing: build 300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 for social rent; zero‑carbon standards; Rent‑to‑Own; longer tenancies; licensing; curb second homes; end rough sleeping; repeal Vagrancy Act.
  - Rural/coastal: bus and rural services funds; universal superfast broadband and wider mobile coverage; coastal change fund.

- Policing, justice and rights
  - £1bn for community policing; public‑health approach to serious violence; £500m for youth services; Online Crime Agency; reform stop and search; replace Police and Crime Commissioners with local boards.
  - Reduce reoffending: more prison officers; presumption against short sentences; decriminalise possession for personal use; Women’s Justice Board; fair disclosure rules; strong rehabilitation on release.
  - Rights: protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; restore Legal Aid (£500m); halt police facial recognition; data/AI ethics code; no‑fault divorce; cohabiting rights; comprehensive equality measures incl. gender recognition reform, BSL Act, period poverty action, parental leave reform and pay‑gap transparency.

- Immigration and asylum
  - End the hostile environment; 28‑day limit on detention; move visa policy out of the Home Office to specialist departments; flexible work and post‑study visas; lower/waived fees; fair family rules.
  - Asylum: right to work after 3 months; resettle 10,000 vulnerable refugees annually and 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years; faster, higher‑quality decisions; free English lessons; longer move‑on period.

- Foreign policy and defence
  - Support multilateral institutions; maintain 0.7% aid with stronger focus on climate, gender and human rights; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; tighter arms export controls (including suspensions to rights‑abusing conflicts).
  - Parliamentary votes on military action; NATO 2% spending; bolster cyber capabilities; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent (reduced fleet, altered posture).

TEXT_F:
Summary of key proposals (ideology-free)

Economy and investment
- Create a Sustainable Investment Board; launch a £400bn National Transformation Fund, including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund.
- Establish a National Investment Bank with Regional Development Banks and a Post Bank to expand lending, especially to SMEs and communities.
- Tighten financial regulation to shift capital from polluting assets to green investment; change London Stock Exchange listing rules to require climate responsibility.

Climate, energy and industry
- Target most emissions reductions by 2030; create 1m climate jobs.
- Deliver ~90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon sources by 2030; expand offshore/onshore wind, solar, tidal; retain new nuclear; ban fracking.
- Retrofit almost all homes to high efficiency; roll out heat pumps, district heat networks, storage and grid upgrades.
- Impose a windfall tax on oil firms; support a just transition for energy workers.
- Bring energy and water into public ownership; create a UK National Energy Agency and 14 Regional Energy Agencies.
- Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; support steel, hydrogen, CCS; build gigafactories; develop plastics remanufacturing; green public procurement.

Transport
- Bring rail and buses into public ownership; reinstate cut bus routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils control services.
- Nationwide rail electrification; HS2 to Scotland; “Crossrail for the North”; expand rail freight.
- Increase cycling/walking funding; aim to end new combustion car sales by 2030; invest in EV charging and zero‑emission public fleets.

Environment, food and animal welfare
- New Climate and Environment Emergency Bill; Clean Air Act; increased flood defence funding.
- Legally binding nature recovery targets; major tree planting; stronger protected areas; environmental tribunal.
- Producer responsibility for waste; deposit return schemes.
- Establish a Right to Food; halve food bank use in a year and end need in three years; net‑zero food production by 2040.
- Strengthen animal welfare, including ending certain wildlife culls and harmful trapping.

Public finances and services
- Fund services via fairer taxation (higher rates only on top earners; no VAT rise); major anti‑avoidance drive.
- Presumption to insource public services; phase out PFI; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for estates.
- Public sector pay: year‑one 5% rise and above‑inflation increases thereafter.

Health and social care
- Health spending to rise by 4.3% annually; end outsourcing; invest in capital, IT and diagnostics; free prescriptions and basic dentistry.
- Expand mental health access, modernise facilities, boost children’s services.
- Create a National Care Service; free personal care for older people; cap lifetime care costs; improve care worker pay and conditions; raise Carer’s Allowance.

Education and skills
- Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; extend paid maternity leave to 12 months.
- More school funding; class sizes capped at 30 in primaries; scrap SATs; arts premium; stronger SEND support.
- Bring academies/free schools under local oversight; free school meals for all primary pupils.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 3 and six years at Levels 4–6); abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; post‑qualification admissions.
- Climate Apprenticeships funded via reformed levy.

Work, rights and corporate governance
- Real Living Wage of at least £10/hour for all 16+; ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral bargaining; ban unpaid internships.
- Target 32‑hour average full‑time week within a decade with no loss of pay.
- Create a Workers’ Protection Agency; require one‑third worker‑elected directors; Inclusive Ownership Funds in large firms.

Policing, justice and security
- Recruit additional police and PCSOs; restore neighbourhood policing.
- Reunify probation; restore legal aid; presumption against short prison sentences; strengthen victims’ rights.
- Overhaul cybersecurity; review border controls.

Housing
- Build over 1m social homes in a decade; at least 150k/yr by end of term, including 100k council homes; end Right to Buy.
- Rent controls; end no‑fault evictions; national licensing and standards; zero‑carbon homes standard; £1bn fire safety fund; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Create a Sovereign Land Trust; “use it or lose it” powers on stalled sites.

Digital, culture, media, sport, gambling
- Free full‑fibre broadband nationwide by 2030 via a public provider; Charter of Digital Rights.
- Cultural Capital Fund; arts premium; media plurality reforms; protect free TV licences for over‑75s.
- Football governance reforms; curb gambling advertising; new Gambling Act with limits and levy.

Migration, refugees, social security, equalities
- End hostile policies; end indefinite detention; close specified detention centres; protect family reunion; declaratory rights for EU nationals; safe routes and right to work for refugees.
- Replace Universal Credit; interim fixes (end five‑week wait and sanctions; scrap benefit cap and two‑child limit; raise Local Housing Allowance).
- Strengthen disability rights and benefits; increase Carer’s Allowance.
- Maintain pension triple lock; keep state pension age at 66; fair remedy for affected women; transparent pensions dashboard.

Constitution and governance
- Abolish the House of Lords, replacing it with an elected Senate after a constitutional convention.
- Votes at 16; automatic voter registration; repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; stricter lobbying/donations rules; extend FOI.

Foreign policy and defence
- War Powers Act; increase diplomatic capacity; human‑rights‑led trade and arms export controls; climate diplomacy; recognise Palestine within a two‑state framework.
- Maintain NATO commitment and spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; renew the nuclear deterrent; support veterans; publish defence industrial and shipbuilding strategies.

Brexit
- Negotiate a customs‑union‑based deal with close single market alignment and put it to a confirmatory referendum alongside remain within six months; implement the result; guarantee citizens’ rights.
